product_family: Meeting recording infrastructure API (bots, on-device SDKs, calendar data, transcripts)

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: Trust Center Resources list 'Hyperdoc Inc. SOC 2 Type 2 Report 2025.pdf' labelled 'SOC 2 Type 2 Report (2025)' (access on request), and the Compliance section displays 'SOC 2'.

certifications.name: ISO 27001:2022
certifications.proof_quote: Compliance section lists 'ISO 27001:2022' and Resources include an 'ISO 27001 ISMS Certificate' available for request.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: "Recall.ai is HIPAA compliant, which means that companies can now use Recall to securely capture conversations that contain protected health information (PHI)." BAA available on request. Trust Center also lists 'HIPAA'.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: Trust Center Compliance section lists 'GDPR'; a Data Processing Agreement with SCC-based US transfer language is published.

certifications.name: CCPA
certifications.proof_quote: Trust Center Compliance section displays 'CCPA' with a 'COMPLIANT' badge.

certifications.name: Penetration Test (Oneleet, 2025)
certifications.proof_quote: Trust Center Resources list 'Recall_Oneleet_PenetrationTest_2025.pdf' labelled 'Penetration Test 2025' (available on request).

certifications.name: Public bug bounty (HackerOne / Bugcrowd)
certifications.proof_quote: No public bug bounty program found on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, or the vendor's own security pages. Security testing is handled via third-party penetration testing (Oneleet) rather than a crowdsourced bounty.

privacy.ai_training_note: Vendor explicitly states it does not train on customer data: "Recall.ai does not use Customer Data for the purpose of training or fine-tuning machine learning or artificial intelligence models." (docs.recall.ai). DPA distinguishes Company Usage Data, which may be processed to 'optimize and maintain performance of the Services', from customer personal data.
privacy.data_region: Primary processing in the United States (AWS). Subprocessor list shows AWS hosting in US, EU, JP; Datadog logging US/EU; Svix webhooks EU. Privacy policy: personal information is stored and processed in the United States.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: Data encrypted at rest on AWS infrastructure ('Data encryption utilized' control listed; DPA confirms encryption at rest via AWS).

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: 'Data transmission encrypted' listed under Product security controls.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Third-party penetration test by Oneleet, 2025 report available on request.

security.name: Access controls
security.value: Encryption key access restricted, unique account authentication enforced, production application access restricted (Infrastructure security controls).

security.name: Resilience
security.value: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery plans established and tested; cybersecurity insurance maintained; documented Incident Response Plan.

security.name: Data retention controls
security.value: Configurable retention via API, including zero data retention (recording_config.retention = null). Default retention is indefinite for accounts created after June 12, 2025; 7 days for older accounts.

security.name: Bug bounty
security.value: No public crowdsourced bug bounty program found.

products.name: Meeting Bot API
products.data_scope: A bot joins video calls (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams) to capture audio, video, transcripts, chat, and metadata. Media stored on Recall servers per retention config; explicit recording consent model.
products.notes: Best when explicit recording consent is needed or for building AI meeting agents. Recordings flow through Recall infrastructure (US/AWS).

products.name: Desktop Recording SDK
products.data_scope: Records video conferences and in-person meetings via a desktop app, on-device, without a bot joining the call ('stealthier' capture). Data scope depends on customer integration and chosen upload/retention.
products.notes: On-device capture reduces server-side footprint vs the bot API; still subject to the same platform retention controls when media is uploaded.

products.name: Calendar API
products.data_scope: Pulls meeting metadata including participant emails, meeting titles, and scheduling data to enrich recordings. Handles PII (attendee emails).
products.notes: Increases PII surface (participant emails); covered by the DPA and subprocessor list.

products.name: Mobile Recording SDK
products.data_scope: Records in-person meetings, cell phone calls, and VOIP calls from mobile devices.
products.notes: Marked 'Coming Soon' on the homepage; compliance scope not yet separately documented. Treat as roadmap.

compare.pricing_model: Usage-based: 5 free recording hours, then $0.50/hour with volume discounts; enterprise plans available. Quoted 99.9% SLA.
compare.data_residency: US-primary (AWS). EU and JP hosting present in the subprocessor list; no documented customer-selectable single-region residency guarantee. Configurable / zero data retention available.

flags: Legal entity is Hyperdoc Inc.; SOC 2 report is issued under that name (matches, not a discrepancy).
Not to be confused with getrecall.ai or recall.it, an unrelated personal-knowledge 'Recall' app. This report covers recall.ai, the meeting recording API.
Default data retention is now indefinite for accounts created after June 12, 2025 (previously 7 days); meeting media persists indefinitely unless retention is explicitly configured.
Certification report PDFs (SOC 2, ISO 27001 cert, pentest) are gated behind 'Request access' and were not opened directly; existence and labels verified on the public Trust Center index.
No public bug bounty; security testing relies on third-party pentest (Oneleet).
